html:
The Coquille are a Native people of the southern Oregon coast, named for the Coquille River, which reaches the Pacific at Bandon. Two groups lived on the river: the Miluk, who spoke a Coosan language, near the mouth, and the Upper Coquille, who spoke an Athabaskan language, upstream. They fished salmon and gathered shellfish, acorns and camas.

Gold miners and settlers flooded the area in the 1850s. After the Rogue River Wars of 1855 and 1856 most survivors were moved north to the Coast Reservation, later the Siletz reservation. The US government ended its recognition of the western Oregon tribes in 1954 and restored the Coquille Indian Tribe in 1989. Their northern neighbours were the Hanis Coos.
